READING

**The numbers first**

*Vantwyn net per season*

| Item | Per season |
|---|---|
| Contract income (400 × £168) | +£67,200 |
| Borage foregone (400 × £71) | −£28,400 |
| Spray replacements (9% × 400 × £210) | −£7,560 |
| Haulage | −£6,900 |
| **Net operational gain over staying home** | **+£24,340** |

Over three seasons that is £73,020.

*Kit value*

Under ORMSCLEUCH the Ravensgate offer yields £96,000 now.
Under TREVANNOCK the kit is worth roughly £20,000 when the permit lapses at the start of 2030, so about 3½ years from now.

Nominal difference in kit proceeds: £96,000 − £20,000 = £76,000 in favour of ORMSCLEUCH.

*Three-season comparison*

TREVANNOCK operational surplus over ORMSCLEUCH: +£73,020
TREVANNOCK kit shortfall against ORMSCLEUCH: −£76,000
**Net: ORMSCLEUCH ahead by roughly £3,000 in nominal terms.**

At even a modest 5 % discount rate, £20,000 received in 3½ years is worth about £16,800 today. Restated in present value, ORMSCLEUCH leads by roughly £6,000–£9,000. The three seasons of Vantwyn work do not quite pay for the difference between selling the kit now and holding it to a £20,000 residual.

**Risk**

The 9 % spray figure comes from a real event on the same programme; Vantwyn will not alter it. That is not an insurable contingency — it is a known, fixed characteristic of this customer. Thirty-six replacement colonies per season is £7,560 already included above, but the calculation assumes losses stop at exactly 9 %. A worse year pushes the operational surplus down and narrows or eliminates it. Colony condition also tends to drift downward under repeated exposure to spray-heavy programmes, which could affect honey yields when the colonies return home, a cost that is not captured in the figures at all.

**The kit sale window**

Ravensgate's offer closes 2026-11-28. TREVANNOCK means declining it. There is no indication Ravensgate or anyone else will offer £96,000 again; the lorry's most obvious commercial value depends on the permit that expires on 2030-01-01. If Vantwyn lapsed after season two or three, the sale route narrows and the asset strands at the farm value.

**Coldharbour and Nyefield**

Two growers asking for a quote is genuinely interesting, but it is not a contract. The 100 pallets are already fully committed to Vantwyn's 400 colonies, so any 2028 vale business would require either additional kit, a negotiated release from Vantwyn, or staggered timing — none of which exists yet. This optionality exists only if TREVANNOCK is chosen, but it cannot be valued at a figure that changes the conclusion given how early-stage it is, and the three contracts that originally justified the migratory investment all lapsed without renewal.

**Operational clarity**

The heather and borage operation is already functioning and returned £143,000 last season across 640 colonies with no haulage, no spray exposure, and no counter-party risk. ORMSCLEUCH allows full management attention to that business rather than splitting it between a marginal pollination contract and the core honey enterprise.

**Summary**

On the numbers alone ORMSCLEUCH is marginally better and the margin widens once time value is applied. On risk it is substantially better because the spray exposure is non-negotiable and structurally depresses the Vantwyn net. On simplicity it is better. The only genuine argument for TREVANNOCK is the vale presence and the Coldharbour/Nyefield prospect, but that prospect is uncontracted and the previous three contracts all failed to renew — there is no track record here that warrants carrying the downside.

READING
  The three-season Vantwyn surplus (£73,020) falls short of the difference between the Ravensgate sale price now (£96,000) and the post-permit residual (£20,000), leaving TREVANNOCK roughly £3,000 behind in nominal terms and £6,000–9,000 behind in present value before any account is taken of the spray risk, which is real, non-negotiable and could worsen; the Coldharbour/Nyefield interest is promising but entirely uncontracted and the prior track record of the migratory side is three lapsed contracts in a row.

CALL
  ORMSCLEUCH

GROUNDS
  The Ravensgate sale recovers more in cash today than three seasons of Vantwyn work can earn above the opportunity cost of the borage, the spray losses and the haulage, and that deficit only grows once the time value of the money and the uninsurable spray risk are placed in the scales.
